88forn: Quentin "Ghost" Forn came up the line in the rain with a child's drawing of a horse and nothing else. The sergeant wrote him down as Private and pointed at the mud.
Day 3: Verdel Ridge was lost. Quentin "Ghost" Forn wrote down the news without trying to explain it.
A parcel came for Quentin "Ghost" Forn that was really meant for another soldier with the same surname. Inside: three pairs of woollen mittens. He put everything back and kept only the wrapping.
At the Chalk Pits, Quentin "Ghost" Forn of the Hegemony and Albin Zgz of the Concord traded insults across the wire for an hour. By the end they were trading recipes.

A direct hit on the trench at R-F8. Quentin "Ghost" Forn was the only one they could still help, and only just. Quentin "Ghost" Forn was killed outright by a direct hit at R-F8. The men dug for an hour and found only his identity disc.

The House of Forn sent Matthias "Rabbit" Forn after Quentin "Ghost" Forn. This time the family packed two pairs of spare socks. News that the Hegemony had taken Hill 304 reached Matthias "Rabbit" Forn during supper. The same stew suddenly tasted better.
Matthias "Rabbit" Forn found an old shopping list inside a coat pocket. Soap, lamp oil, apples. He folded it along the original creases.
A pocket watch went along the bench so everyone could set the time. Matthias "Rabbit" Forn has no watch, but checked it anyway, just to feel included.

Fresh from training, Matthias "Rabbit" Forn still aims the way the instructor said. Today it worked: Dorian Wman, grazed. A bullet clipped Matthias "Rabbit" Forn's helmet at R-F8 and took a strip of scalp with it. He bled into his collar, swore, and lay low. Shot by Yann Spring of the Concord (@spring_7398).
Stitches out, sleeve rolled down. Matthias "Rabbit" Forn is whole again, or near enough for the line.
bri3kcls: "You're late," said the corporal when Quentin "Rabbit" Kcls arrived on Day 8. "Everyone's late. Get a spade."
Quentin "Rabbit" Kcls's spoon vanished during supper. He scratched a mark into a replacement and began keeping a closer eye on the washing bucket.
deutsches_kaiserreich_official: Rafael Official told the sergeant he was a tram conductor. The sergeant said the war needed one of those like it needed a hole in the roof, and put him on sentry.
filip_ogwanga: Rafael "Saint" Ogwanga came from Ashford Vale, where there is a river, a church and no mud at all. He talks about all three as if they were people.
Rafael "Saint" Ogwanga held the mirror while Ulrich Asher shaved. The arrangement survived the shaving but not the comments.
The order named Rafael "Saint" Ogwanga as Lance Corporal. He read it twice, then asked who would take over his watch.

Rafael "Saint" Ogwanga found a blank menu card and wrote the evening ration on it in elaborate handwriting. The bread became 'Bread, in the Army Manner'. Rafael "Saint" Ogwanga walked the captured trenches of Hill 304 and found the enemy's cooking pots still warm. He took a spoon as a souvenir.
Rafael "Saint" Ogwanga had been watching the same gap for an hour. When Leopold "Brick" Moovin crossed it, Rafael "Saint" Ogwanga fired. Leopold "Brick" Moovin was grazed.
Rafael "Saint" Ogwanga's menu now circulates before supper. Someone has requested a wine list. The water bucket has been given a vintage.
Oskar Urfavv of the Concord shouted a joke across the wire at the Chalk Pits. Rafael "Saint" Ogwanga of the Hegemony laughed before remembering not to. Both lines heard it.
Rafael "Saint" Ogwanga saved half a biscuit for later. Later came six minutes afterwards.
hiro.ki353: Felix "Ghost" Hiro arrived on Day 9 and found the section asleep. The welcome had to wait until somebody needed the kettle.
jacobflamberg: Nils Jacobflamber left a sweetheart who has stopped writing behind in Esterhaus and came up the line with a child's drawing of a horse. The men noticed at once that he hums hymns when frightened.
tsafler: Wendel Tsafler came up with a draft of replacements on Day 9. Nobody asked his name until the third night. After that, everyone knew it.
w1ll1am_e: Walter "Ghost" Wllame joined the replacements on Day 9. An old hand checked his pack straps before asking his name.
